notes: No manuscript page number is visible at the head. The pale bottom-left 92 is retained as a margin foliation, with hand attribution left open. No date is written on this page.

The opening says that the selected marked points I′ on X-hat-prime may more generally be chosen in J-tilde disjoint-union I. The next paragraph describes selecting A′ from A(G) and I′ from I disjoint-union J-tilde, with the written definition J-tilde = A-tilde(G) minus A-tilde-prime, and asserts that a resulting special curve is pinned by a new marked graph. The graph is described using the same S vertices and A′ as its edges, marking set I′, the maps in (126), and the original genus application. These are the author’s claims, not results verified in this reading.

The source uses the literal universal sign before courbe spéciale and the literal equals sign before the separate S in sommets. The latter is an abbreviated même/mêmes usage, not an equation supplied by the transcriber. H expands these signs and omits the separate S. The supplied notation table helped compare these handwritten sign forms; it did not provide missing letters.

Both live marked-graph prefixes are small m. The possible abbreviation stops cannot be separated securely from the terminal pen ink of m, so only each stop is doubtful. The preceding cancelled MD candidate remains doubtful independently. No expansion of m is asserted because this sheet does not state one.

The prefix before graphe in en prenant le ... is compact and appears contracted ss-. The alternatives s, sous and x remain because the compressed strokes do not securely resolve every letter. Neither witness’s full sous is silently accepted as certain.

The G′ de G insertion is written above the line and attaches after the prefix-plus-graphe word, before ayant. The long curved line beneath the insertion is its attachment connector, not a strike through the live ayant and not an underline belonging to G′ or G. H’s doubt on ayant is resolved by the visible word and descender.

After the cancelled possible right parenthesis in the set definition, the only live mark is a low comma. The draft consequently leaves the opening parenthesis before où without a live matching close, retaining the cancelled delimiter separately. No closing parenthesis has been supplied for grammatical balance.

The comma after sommets is visible and is retained. The first quoted pts marqués and the later ens de pts marqués use paired raised strokes, not guillemets. No stop is written after ens in the second quotation; the earlier ens. before d’arêtes does have its stop.

The word after the first map in (126) is induit, without final e. The final verb is est, not étant. These written grammatical forms are preserved. The word origine is placed over the rightmost arrow from A-tilde(G) to S: its baseline is close above that shaft and well below the preceding prose baseline, as inspected on the original and native lower half.

The original page and both native halves were viewed line by line. Ten local crops were generated once with LANCZOS enlargement, autocontrast and mild sharpening, without rotation, and all ten were visually inspected. The formula126 crop clips the upper edge of origine, so that complete label and its attachment were read on the original and native lower half; the crop contains the differing induit and the arrows. The blind box for that region includes the complete upper line, label and display. No OCR, external research, TeX compilation or mathematical proof check was performed.

Main inventory clarification: the live m after cancelled MD is on the ordinary baseline and has no separately demonstrated insertion hook. It is inventoried as text; the TeX does not invent an insertion state.

Blind audit confirms the universal sign, the separate equals sign and S before sommets, the live comma after the continued word, and the number (126). It broadens the tiny contracted-prefix alternatives and marks the short article ending and avec/on locally doubtful. The cancelled first prefix remains an uncertain MD candidate; its live replacement is on the baseline, with no independently demonstrated insertion state.
